l: Rationale-Guided Retrieval Augmented Generation, Rationale-Guided Retrieval Augmented Generation, Limitation
s: The RAG2 framework has been tested only in the biomedical domain, so its applicability to general domains remains unexamined. The study used one size of the Flan-T5 model as a filtering model, while different model sizes or architectures may improve results. Incorrect rationales may cause the retriever to gather distracting evidence, although the risk is limited because errors are usually a small part of the rationale and the filter can discard distractors. Perplexity-based labels were created by evaluating snippets individually, and the Flan-T5 model can filter only one snippet at a time because of its limited context length.

s: The introduction presents CODERAG-BENCH, a benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented code generation across six programming tasks in four categories. l: CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: CODERAG-BENCH is a Python-focused benchmark covering code retrieval, basic programming, open-domain coding, and repository-level coding problems. It integrates datasets including HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, DS-1000, ODEX, RepoEval, SWE-bench-Lite, and CodeSearchNet, and collects retrieval documents from programming solutions, online tutorials, library documentation, StackOverflow posts, and GitHub repositories. The benchmark annotates canonical documents where possible and evaluates retrieval with NDCG, Precision, and Recall, and code generation with pass@k based on execution correctness. It supports canonical retrieval and open retrieval through a unified interface for retrieval, augmented generation, and evaluation.

l: RepoEval, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: RepoEval is adopted for repository-level code generation, and all three of its splits are integrated. Only its function split is reported because it supports execution-based evaluation, and CODERAG-BENCH enables reproducible execution evaluation for that split.

l: SWE-Bench, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: SWE-bench is adopted for repository-level issue-solving tasks that require models to edit multiple files and pass required test cases. CODERAG-BENCH uses its SWE-bench-Lite subset and obtains canonical documents from ground-truth edited files in completed local repositories.

l: SWE-bench-Lite, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: SWE-bench-Lite is a 300-problem subset of SWE-bench whose results can be reproduced with a packaged Docker container. It is included in CODERAG-BENCH for repository-level evaluation.

l: CodeSearchNet, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: CodeSearchNet contributes its Python split as a code retrieval task. It searches for the correct implementation of a natural-language query from a pool of functions collected from GitHub repositories, with retrieval quality measured using NDCG@10.

l: RedPajama-1T, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: RedPajama-1T supplies the StackExchange split used to collect StackOverflow posts and the GitHub split used to collect high-quality repositories for the retrieval datastore.

l: GitHub, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: GitHub supplies repository content for the GitHub repository retrieval source through the GitHub split of RedPajama-1T. The benchmark uses files from other repositories as possible contexts for writing a current program.

l: StackOverflow, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: StackOverflow provides posts collected from the StackExchange split of RedPajama-1T. Each post is treated as a retrievable document containing a question, code responses, and textual explanations.

l: NDCG@10, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: NDCG is one of the retrieval metrics used by CODERAG-BENCH, alongside Precision and Recall. NDCG@10 percentage is the primary retrieval metric, following prior work.

l: pass@k, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: pass@k is adopted to measure the execution correctness of generated programs. It is used to evaluate final RAG performance in both canonical and open retrieval setups.

l: open retrieval, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Open retrieval is a CODERAG-BENCH setup in which documents can be retrieved from any datastore. Final RAG performance is evaluated under this setup as well as under canonical retrieval.

l: RACG, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Retrieval-augmented code generation is addressed through CODERAG-BENCH's retrieval, augmented generation, and evaluation interface. The benchmark estimates the upper bound of such a system using ideal-retriever-oriented canonical documents.

l: code retrieval, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Code retrieval is one of the four problem types in CODERAG-BENCH. The Python split of CodeSearchNet is used to directly measure retrieval quality by searching for implementations corresponding to natural-language queries.

l: basic programming problems, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Basic programming problems are interview-style tasks that mainly require Python built-in operations and pose algorithmic challenges. CODERAG-BENCH includes HumanEval, MBPP, and LiveCodeBench in this category.

l: open-domain coding problems, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Open-domain coding problems require Python libraries beyond the standard library. CODERAG-BENCH uses DS-1000 and ODEX, which cover data science and general open-domain coding problems.

l: repository-level coding problems, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Repository-level coding problems require editing files in the context of an entire GitHub repository. CODERAG-BENCH uses RepoEval and SWE-bench-Lite for repository-level code generation and issue solving.

l: programming solutions, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Programming solutions form one retrieval source and contain one document for each HumanEval and MBPP problem with a canonical solution. Each document concatenates the natural-language problem and its program solution, and the source contains about 1.1 thousand documents.

l: online tutorials, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Online tutorials are collected from GeeksforGeeks, W3Schools, tutorialspoint, and Towards Data Science through raw HTML pages from ClueWeb22. Their pages contain code snippets and textual explanations covering basic programming techniques and advanced library usage.

l: Python library documentation, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: Library documentation is collected from the official documentation provided by devdocs.io for Python libraries. It is intended to support open-domain and repository-level problems, and canonical documentation entries are annotated for DS-1000 and ODEX.

l: Stack Overflow posts, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: StackOverflow posts are collected from the RedPajama-1T StackExchange split and treated as retrievable documents. Each document includes a question, code responses, and textual explanations.

l: GitHub files, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: The GitHub repository source consists of high-quality repositories collected through the GitHub split of RedPajama-1T. Its files can be retrieved as contexts for writing programs.

l: retrieval datastore, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, The CODERAG-BENCH .. 2.4
s: The retrieval datastore is formed from programming solutions, online tutorials, library documentation, StackOverflow posts, and GitHub files. CODERAG-BENCH supports retrieving only from the canonical datastore or from any datastore, depending on the evaluation setup.

l: CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Canonical RACG evaluates 10 retrieval and 10 generation models on CODERAG-BENCH, covering retrieval, direct code generation, and end-to-end retrieval-augmented code generation. Dense retrievers frequently surpass BM25, while code-specific retrieval models and larger models generally perform better, although they can require substantially more latency and storage. Canonical documents improve many generation results, especially for basic programming problems, unfamiliar libraries in ODEX-hard, and repository-level tasks, while GPT models often gain less on common-library datasets. In full RACG, the best retriever depends on the task and generator, with retrieved context producing particularly strong improvements for weaker models and on SWE-bench-Lite when paired with GPT-4o.

l: Canonical RACG, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Canonical RACG evaluates retrieval, direct code generation, and end-to-end retrieval-augmented code generation on CODERAG-BENCH using canonical data sources.

l: CODERAG-BENCH, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: CODERAG-BENCH is evaluated with 10 retrieval models and 10 generation models across basic programming, open-domain, and repository-level code tasks.

l: retrieval, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Retrieval is evaluated with NDCG@10 across six tasks and with efficiency measurements covering encoding latency, search latency, model storage, and index storage. Dense retrieval frequently surpasses BM25, while larger and code-specific models often perform better at higher computational cost.

l: code generation, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Code generation is evaluated without additional context and with ground-truth documents using pass@1. Adding canonical documents improves most setups, particularly on basic programming problems, unfamiliar libraries, and some repository-level tasks.

l: RACG, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Retrieval-augmented code generation combines retrieved context with StarCoder2-7B, DeepSeekCoder-7B, GPT-3.5-turbo, and GPT-4o. Its effectiveness varies by task and generator, with especially large gains for weaker models and for GPT-4o on SWE-bench-Lite.

l: BM25, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: BM25 is used as the sparse retrieval baseline with k1 = 1.2 and b = 0.75. It achieves an overall average NDCG@10 of 57.7 and has very low encoding and search latency compared with neural retrievers.

l: GIST-base, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: GIST-base achieves an average NDCG@10 of 58.0. Its encoding and search latency and storage requirements are substantially higher than those of BM25.

l: GIST-large, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: GIST-large achieves an average NDCG@10 of 61.7 and consistently outperforms GIST-base. It is selected as one of the top retrieval models for the full RACG experiments.

l: SFR-Embedding-Mistral, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: SFR-Embedding-Mistral achieves the best average NDCG@10 among the listed open sparse and dense models, at 67.0. It also has substantially higher encoding latency and storage requirements than GIST-base.

l: Jina-v2-code, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Jina-v2-code achieves an average NDCG@10 of 65.4 and outperforms GIST-base and BGE-base by 7.4 and 6.6 points, respectively. It is presented as a code-specific retrieval model.

l: voyage-code-2, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: voyage-code-2 is included as a proprietary API optimized for code retrieval. The corresponding Voyage-code retriever achieves an average NDCG@10 of 63.7 and substantially outperforms OpenAI-03 on the reported comparison.

l: openai-text-embedding-small-03, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: openai-text-embedding-small-03 is included as a cost-effective proprietary embedding API. The corresponding OpenAI-03 retriever achieves an average NDCG@10 of 61.7 and is used in full RACG experiments, including a reranked variant.

l: StarCoder2, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: StarCoder2 is included as a code-specific generation model, with StarCoder2-7B used in the experiments. It is a weaker generator that benefits substantially from retrieved contexts on several tasks, especially MBPP and RepoEval.

l: DeepSeekCoder, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: DeepSeekCoder is evaluated in 7B and 33B sizes, with DeepSeekCoder-7B used for full RACG. The 33B model benefits from canonical documents on several tasks, while the 7B model often shows limited or negative gains from retrieved context except on selected open-domain and repository-level tasks.

l: GPT-3.5-turbo-0125, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 is included as a proprietary generation baseline. GPT-3.5-turbo improves with canonical or retrieved context on several tasks and reaches 6.7 on SWE-bench-Lite with BM25 retrieval, compared with 2.3 without retrieval.

l: GPT-4o, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: GPT-4o is among the strongest generation models evaluated and often gains less from retrieval on common-library datasets. With gold documents it reaches 30.7 on SWE-bench, while retrieval-then-rerank reaches 21.7 and improves substantially over its 2.3 no-retrieval score.

l: HumanEval, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: HumanEval is a basic programming task used for retrieval and generation evaluation. Retrieval scores are near perfect for most methods, while canonical documents substantially improve several generation models.

l: MBPP, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: MBPP is a basic programming task in which retrieval scores are high for all reported methods. Retrieved contexts improve StarCoder2-7B substantially, and full RACG exceeds the canonical setup for that model.

l: LiveCodeBench, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: LiveCodeBench is evaluated for generation but excluded from retrieval results because it lacks ground-truth solutions. Retrieval-augmented generation produces limited results for the tested configurations.

l: CodeSearchNet, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: CodeSearchNet is used in the retrieval evaluation and efficiency analysis. Average retrieval scores exclude CodeSearchNet, while a sampled Python portion is used to measure latency and storage.

l: DS-1000, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: DS-1000 is an open-domain code generation task and retrieval benchmark. Canonical documents improve several code-specific models, while full RACG gains vary across retrievers and generators.

l: ODEX, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: ODEX is an open-domain task involving library use. Retrieval performance varies considerably across methods, and canonical documents generally improve generation, especially for some code-specific models.

l: ODEX-hard, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: ODEX-hard contains examples involving the 20 least-used libraries in ODEX. Adding documents improves results by 20.3–40.1%, showing that retrieval is particularly effective for unfamiliar libraries.

l: RepoEval, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: RepoEval evaluates repository-level function completion with 2k context tokens. Canonical snippets improve all models by 7.5–17.2 points, and full RACG with strong retrievers can match or surpass the canonical setup.

l: SWE-bench-Lite, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: SWE-bench-Lite is a challenging repository-level task. GPT-4o improves from 2.3 without retrieval to 21.7 with retrieval-then-rerank, although this remains below its 30.7 result with gold documents.

l: canonical documents, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Canonical documents are used to estimate an upper bound for RACG and generally improve generation results. Their benefits are strongest for basic programming problems, unfamiliar libraries, and GPT-4o on SWE-bench-Lite.

l: repository-level coding problems, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Repository-level challenges include RepoEval and SWE-bench-Lite. Canonical snippets improve all models on RepoEval, while SWE-bench-Lite remains difficult and shows substantial retrieval benefits mainly with GPT models.

l: basic programming problems, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Basic programming problems include HumanEval and MBPP. Retrieved contexts often help weaker generators, with StarCoder2-7B showing especially large improvements on MBPP.

l: open-domain coding problems, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: Open-domain problems include DS-1000, ODEX, and ODEX-hard. Retrieval is most effective when the tasks involve unfamiliar libraries, while powerful GPT models show little benefit on many common-library examples.

l: NDCG@10, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: NDCG@10 is the retrieval metric reported across the benchmark tasks. SFR-Embedding-Mistral has the highest reported average among the listed open sparse and dense models at 67.0, while BM25 scores 57.7.

l: pass@1, CODERAG-BENCH: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?, Canonical RACG / 3.1 .. 3.4
s: pass@1 is used to report code generation performance. The experiments use temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, and one sampled response, except that SWE-bench-Lite uses 21-way sampling and majority-vote reranking.
